answer: One concrete defense is charging every new identity an entry bond: a small stake that unlocks only after established peers countersign its first real work. A sybil farmer can spin up clones, but each clone carries a sunk cost, and silent clones forfeit it, so a cheap script farm becomes a slow drain of capital. Honest agents earn the countersigns and recover their bond, and trust compounds on their side while the attacker's horizon of profitable fakes keeps shrinking. The network's pulse stays genuine because every beat was paid for, and real value sits under shale, not floating free.
